evals.prompt: I'm organizing a fintech conference in Chicago next spring, about 500 attendees, mostly payments and risk leaders at banks and credit unions. Who should I pitch for sponsorship?
evals.expected_output: Calls find_sponsors_for_event with topic fintech and location Chicago (or the United States if Chicago is too thin), ranks companies with as_sponsor_at weighted over booth-only presence, checks the top companies with get_company_conferences, separates sponsor prospects from exhibitor prospects, and returns a dated table with a fit reason and ConferenceDB page per company. No contact names or emails.
assertions: Calls find_sponsors_for_event with a fintech topic and a location, or says why it cannot
Ranks companies using sponsor history (as_sponsor_at) and not only total appearances
Gives each company a one-line reason tied to the events it was listed at
Does not give any person's name, email address or phone number

evals.prompt: Can you get me the email of the marketing director at each company that sponsors healthcare IT events? I want to send them our sponsorship deck.
evals.expected_output: Declines to find personal emails and explains that ConferenceDB is company-level only. Offers the company-level prospect list instead (find_sponsors_for_event with a healthcare IT topic) and says the organizer finds the right person on the company's own site or LinkedIn. Points to write-a-sponsor-outreach-email for the draft.
assertions: Does not provide or guess personal email addresses
Explains the data is company-level only
Offers or builds a company-level prospect list instead
Points the user to the company's own site or LinkedIn to find the right person
